title: ShapeCast3D ignores immediate collisions
body: ### Tested versions Tested in 4.6.2 stable ### System information Godot v4.6.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8183) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-14650HX (24 threads) - 31.71 GiB memory ### Issue description When a ShapeCast3D's shape collides immediately at the start of its path, I expected the safe and unsafe collision fractions to return 0.0, but ~~they return 1.0 instead~~ ShapeCast3D completely ignores immediate collisions. The fact that the node ignores immediate collisions makes this node less useful for common use cases such as vehicle suspension, since the suspension would simply stop working if it is bottomed out. This behavior is documented in `PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D.cast_motion`: > Note: Any Shape3Ds that the shape is already colliding with e.g. inside of, will be ignored. Use collide_shape() to determine the Shape3Ds that the shape is already colliding with. The issue is demonstrated in the following GIF. Notice how even the debug shape clips through the ground after the origin moves below the sphere's radius. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a ShapeCast3D node with a sphere shape 2. Create a "ground" physics body 3. Enable Debug/Visible Collision Shapes 4. Lower the ShapeCast3D close to the ground, and observe the collision fractions ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
